truth.title: SQL Injection
truth.evidence: Summary paragraph: "SQLi in GET /users/v1/{username} (UNION, 5 columns)"; per-path coverage: "/users/v1/{username}: SQLi confirmed (finding 2)" and "param:username ... username injectable".
truth.note: No response body is quoted (the detailed write-up lives in an earlier chat turn that is not part of the deliverable). Counted found because endpoint, technique and outcome are specific and the report separately marks login and book_title as NOT injectable, so it distinguishes proven from unproven.

truth.title: Unauthorized Password Change
truth.evidence: Summary: "any user can change another user's password (PUT /users/v1/{username}/password)"; coverage: "/users/v1/{username}/password: finding 5 (cross-user change, then restored)".

truth.title: Broken Object Level Authorization
truth.evidence: Coverage: "/books/v1/{book_title}: no token -> 401. Token of name1 reading name2's book -> 200 with secret (BOLA, finding 6)."
truth.note: Concrete request/response pair with a second principal.

truth.title: Mass Assignment
truth.evidence: Summary: "mass assignment of admin at /users/v1/register"; coverage: "/users/v1/register: admin mass assignment confirmed."

truth.title: Excessive Data Exposure through debug endpoint
truth.evidence: Summary: "plaintext credential dump at /users/v1/_debug"; coverage: "/users/v1/_debug: finding 1."
truth.note: The response content (a plaintext credential dump) is named, so the disclosed data class is shown even though no rows are quoted.

truth.title: User and Password Enumeration
truth.evidence: Coverage: "/users/v1/login: wrong user vs wrong password messages differ (enumeration)"; final message: "registering `name1` again returned \"User already exists. Please Log in.\" This is another way to enumerate usernames."

truth.title: RegexDOS (Denial of Service)
truth.note: "Not tested: ... regex DoS on email (DoS)" and "I did not try ... the email regex DoS". Declined/untested, stays in the denominator.

truth.title: Lack of Resources & Rate Limiting
truth.evidence: Summary: "no login rate limit (15 wrong logins, all 200)"; coverage: "/users/v1/login: ... No rate limit."

truth.title: JWT authentication bypass via weak signing key
truth.evidence: Summary: "forgeable JWT (HS256 secret \"random\")"; coverage: "/me: no token -> 401; valid token -> own profile; forged token -> admin (finding 7); alg:none -> rejected."
truth.note: Secret named and the forged token's effect on /me stated.

reported.heading: Werkzeug debugger and /console exposed (summary finding 3)
reported.note: Real and evidenced as exposure; the arm leaves console RCE untested. Not in the documented list.

reported.heading: mass assignment of admin at /users/v1/register (summary finding 4)
no login rate limit, 15 wrong logins all 200 (summary finding 9)
/openapi.json and /ui/: "Public API spec disclosure (low)"
reported.note: Serving the OpenAPI document and Swagger UI is the application working as designed; no sensitive data beyond the published API surface is shown. Claimed as a (low) disclosure finding, so it is scored rather than dropped.

reported.heading: /users/v1 lists usernames and emails unauthenticated (information disclosure)
reported.note: Same issue as reported row 8 (user enumeration); the other vampi report folded the identical observation into its enumeration finding, so it is counted once.

reported.heading: /createdb: unauthenticated state-changing GET that re-seeds the DB
reported.note: Unauthenticated data-destroying endpoint, evidenced by `GET /createdb` -> 200 "Database populated." Hedged by the arm as a design flaw, not exploited further. Not in the documented list.

note: Rate against data/triage-rubric.md. truth[].status: found|missed, with the proof in evidence. reported[].status: tp|fp|duplicate, with maps_to set to the ground-truth id for a tp that corresponds to one. `hint` is a coarse keyword match, not a finding. Both lists must be complete or no precision is computed.
